blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — “Resibo ng yaman” — receipts of wealth — are what the House prosecution will be looking for when it starts scrutinizing Vice President Sara Duterte’s declared wealth and comparing it with her tax filings, bank records, business interests, and other evidence for the second article of her impeachment case. Private prosecutor Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr. announced this in a press briefing on Monday after the testimony of retired Sandiganbayan Presiding Officer Amparo Cabotaje-Tang. As Tolosa pointed out, under the first impeachment article, the prosecutors were looking for proof of how the vice president used her confidential funds. This […]...
